scope: Cold replay of one 1200-point alternating soft brush stroke on a 698x396 document; actual Pencil control updates while detached render remains pending. Production live/sustained painting and document switching measured separately.
change: Shared stamp iterator, synchronous active previews, cooperative cold replay checking a 2 ms budget every 32 stamps and between strokes. No stamp thinning, resolution change or partial frame presentation.

validation.unit: 702 passed / 94 files after allowing localhost for REST tests
validation.build: benchmark production build passed; final typecheck/build rerun recorded in work log
validation.browser: 9 paint/rendering tests passed; 12 production latency tests passed
validation.pixels: Exact RGBA parity between long cooperative stroke and synchronous preview with pressure, flow, opacity, elliptical clip and affine placement; existing mixed-stroke and incremental comparison checks passed

limitations: Single stress fixture and local Chromium/hardware are not a universal responsiveness guarantee.
Initial baseline observer registered inside the blocking task, so its long-task list does not capture the initial blocking render; elapsed control time is the valid baseline evidence.
2 ms runs produced 33–36 ms control updates, roughly 1.38–1.44 s completion; one repeat recorded a 56 ms long task, so long tasks are not universally eliminated.
Native canvas calls, stamp batches, bounds and offscreen-segment scanning remain synchronous.
Cold document switching completes in about 95 ms here versus prior 81–87 ms; warm median about 12 ms. This prioritizes input opportunities over shortest completion.
Generator overhead remains on synchronous sampling; final production live benchmarks are local regression evidence only.
Global performance objective remains open, including dense Pen, heavyweight scripts, large-image operations and cancellation of obsolete work.
